fixes.explanation: They say it themselves: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’” (Mark 11:31). They can see the trap closing before they step in it. I do that with a text I'm about to send: type it, read it back, and see the reply coming before I ever hit send.

Nothing about an arrest comes up in their huddle. They say, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’” (Mark 11:31). The question they expect is about believing John.

That's not the question they expect. Their words are, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’” (Mark 11:31). The question they expect Jesus to ask is about believing John.

They answer, “We do not know.” (Mark 11:33). They had two doors and chose to say neither. Honestly, I've given that shrug in a staff meeting when both answers got me in trouble, and it never helped me either.
They don't say that. In their huddle they said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’” (Mark 11:31). What they actually say is, “We do not know.” (Mark 11:33).

Jesus says the man “…rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.” (Mark 12:1). So the owner rents the vineyard out and travels away. Remember who's in that vineyard, because it matters soon.
He does plant it and set it up, but that's not where the verse stops. Jesus says he “…rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.” (Mark 12:1). He rents it out and goes away.
Right, he doesn't stop. Jesus says, “He sent still another, and this one they killed. He sent many others; some they beat and others they killed.” (Mark 12:5). It's a heavy part of the story.
The tenants say, “This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.” (Mark 12:7). They know exactly who he is. I think that's a dark plan.

The watchtower is in the story, because the owner built one (Mark 12:1). But the verse doesn't name it here. Jesus says, “So they seized the son, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.” (Mark 12:8).

The Scripture says, “This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes…” (Mark 12:11). So the stone's new place is from the Lord. The Scripture also calls it marvelous. That's the end of what Jesus quotes.

The text says, “But fearing the crowd, they left Him and went away.” (Mark 12:12). Back in their huddle about John, they were “…afraid of the people…” (Mark 11:32). Fear of the crowd is what holds them back here.
